title: Claude doesn't lose track when the conversation gets long
blurb: Long conversations get shortened automatically to free up room, and details get dropped when that happens. This writes down where you'd got to first, so nothing important disappears.
newcomerProblem: After a long session Claude suddenly forgets what you were doing and starts redoing work you already finished.
tryThisExplain: After a long session, ask Claude that to pick up exactly where you left off.
explain: Claude can only hold so much of a conversation at once. When it fills up, older parts get squeezed into a short summary, and specifics get lost — which files you touched, what you already tried, what didn't work. This notices that moment coming and writes the important parts to a file first, so they can be read back afterwards.
honestLimit: It saves what can be read from your project — changed files, recent commits, the branch. It can't save the parts of the conversation that were only ever spoken about.
uninstallNote: The note file it wrote is left where it is, in case you still want it.
